# Feed Flow!: Baby Feeding, Growth & Health Tracker for iPhone

> One calm app for breastfeeding, formula, pumping and solids, WHO growth references, allergens, reactions, medicines, vaccines and vitamin D.

Feed Flow! is built in Norway by Zeolite and is available on the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6782075454

Feed Flow! keeps feeding, growth and baby health records in one place. A prepared-bottle countdown can remain visible on the lock screen. FlowCast uses the baby's own feeding history to suggest a likely next-feed window; it is a planning guide, not a schedule or medical prediction. The baby's data stays in the parent's own iCloud.

## Feeding

- **Breastfeeding and pumping:** log nursing, pumping, expressed milk and formula together without judgement.
- **Bottle countdown:** the countdown runs from when you make the bottle. The default is one hour for formula and two hours for pumped milk, and you can change it in Settings. It also shows on the lock screen. It is a memory aid, not a safety sensor.
- **Today at a glance:** nursing, bottles, pumping, water and solids all appear in the day's timeline. The milk total counts formula, pumped milk and nursing (nursing as an estimate). Solids and water are shown separately.
- **Formula brands:** compare formulas side by side by milk base, protein, the tummy worry they address, stage and vitamin D, using the values on the label. You can enter your own product. Feed Flow does not rank or recommend brands.
- **FlowCast and meal planning:** with Premium, after about four days of logged feeds FlowCast shows a likely window for the next feed and the day ahead. After a few bottles, the amounts you usually pour appear as one-tap buttons, which can help families prepare closer to what is needed and reduce waste.
- **Caregiver sharing:** invite everyone who looks after your baby. They log through their own iCloud, and Premium adds a detailed activity feed.

## Growth and development

- Track weight, height and head circumference against WHO growth references.
- Weight, height and head circumference can be logged for free. Premium shows them against the WHO band with the percentile named.
- Record developmental milestones with dates, notes and photos.
- Premium includes full growth curves and longer analytics.
- WHO reference source: https://www.who.int/tools/child-growth-standards/standards

## Baby health

- Track nine major allergen groups, food attempts and later reaction notes.
- Log medicines and vaccination dates without dosage or schedule advice.
- Log vitamin D drops and vitamin D listed on the formula label.
- Keep health notes beside feeding and growth for conversations with a pediatrician, health nurse or lactation professional.
- Feed Flow does not diagnose allergies, assess causation, calculate medicine doses or replace professional care.

## Reports and pricing

Everyday logging is free. Premium adds the next-feed time, the day-ahead view, the activity feed, the vitamin D meter, full history, growth curves and Baby Reports. A separate Reports Pass is also available. Current regional prices and purchase options are shown in the App Store.

## Ambassador program

Eligible parent creators, mom influencers, IBCLCs, lactation consultants and feeding professionals can apply for a single-level ambassador program. Accepted ambassadors earn 35–50% commission on net profit from eligible app sales directly attributed to their own link or code. The exact rate, net-profit definition, products, attribution, reporting and payout terms are confirmed in an agreement before participation. There are no recruitment commissions or downlines. Earnings and acceptance are not guaranteed.

Apply or share: https://tryfeedflow.app/ambassador

## Privacy and medical boundary

Feed Flow! is a record-keeping app, not a medical device. It does not diagnose conditions, recommend medicine doses or replace a pediatrician, pharmacist, midwife, health nurse or lactation professional. Baby data lives on the phone and in the parent's own iCloud. Website analytics are separate from baby records.
